Implemented the focused Home and Horizon Watch changes locally. Nothing was deployed or tested on the Vizio. The Pico, SmartCast seeking, player bridge, and authentication protocol were unchanged.

Findings and fixes

  • Pairing: Home attempted a pairing-session check on every HTTPS launch and opened the modal after any unsuccessful response. The checked-in Home assets configuration has no pairing API, which explains why an unavailable service could produce a modal with no code. Home now opens pairing only after the API explicitly returns not_authorized. An outage leaves Home usable without marking the TV authorized. If pairing is required but code creation fails, the code stays hidden and the error gives a next step. A failed optional session rotation no longer triggers pairing unless authorization is explicitly rejected. The exact response from the deployed TV session remains unverified.
  • Home scrolling: Focus used “nearest” scrolling, so reaching the upper row did not restore the hero. D-pad Up to the header now sets the Home scroll container to 0 and preserves the tile to return to on Down. Chromium down/up traversal passed at all three requested sizes.
  • Details and artwork: The old details block treated portrait posters as landscape backgrounds. The new cinematic hero uses a fitted landscape backdrop, a contained portrait poster fallback, and a stable no-art fallback. The episode view now shows TMDB stills where available, with readable placeholders.
  • Providers: The former provider “launcher” merely returned to Home. It is removed. Subscription marking remains; a title-matched, US-specific TMDB watch-page action appears only when TMDB supplies a validated link. It is an external page, not a provider-app or title deep link. TMDB says its watch-provider response does not supply full provider deep links. TMDB watch-provider documentation (https://developer.themoviedb.org/reference/tv-series-watch-providers)
  • Subtitles: No saved choice now means Off. Explicit On and Off choices are stored on the Watch origin and carried in player and episode URLs. Returning from the player updates Watch’s preference. A direct Vizio Home exit from the separate player origin cannot synchronize that choice until Watch receives a return; existing English-language URL handling was left intact.

You shouldn't lose your Horizon history, settings, or pairing credentials just from redeploying. Cloudflare Wrangler deployments normally replace the application code and static assets, not browser storage.

Here's what happens to your data:

Watch History

Continue Watching

Subtitle preferences

One important caveat: Horizon's history lives primarily in browser localStorage, not a backed-up server database. Redeploying to the same origins doesn't normally clear it, but browser storage eviction, changing origins, or changing storage schemas can affect it. Home and Watch maintain separate history copies.

Your latest implementation report says the existing history model was preserved, which is encouraging, but it is not a guarantee against an untested migration bug.
